identity.name: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata
native_names: Virreinato del Rio de la Plata
identity.wikipedia: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata

land.text: the Audiencia of Charcas and the governorates of the Rio de la Plata, Paraguay and Tucuman

predecessors.note: 'On 1 August 1776 the king gave Pedro de Cevallos control over the Audiencia of Charcas and the corregimiento of Cuyo'; the viceroyalty was 'formalised' on 27 October 1777.

land.text: the corregimiento of Cuyo, under the Audiencia of Chile

predecessors.note: Cuyo 'was a corregimiento under the Audiencia of Chile' and passed to Cevallos in 1776.

land.text: the United Provinces' shape, which took Montevideo and the Banda Oriental

successors.note: Alvear entered Montevideo after Vigodet's surrender on 17 May 1814 (the infobox's 'Fall of Montevideo: 23 June 1814', the text's 23 May 1814); the page's 'Formally abolished: 1 April 1825' is the date Olañeta died at Tumusla, not a territorial event.
'The Intendency of Paraguay rejected Buenos Aires' authority, but declared independence a year later.'

land.text: Upper Peru: the intendancies of Chuquisaca, La Paz, Potosi and Cochabamba, plus Moxos and Chiquitos

successors.note: Upper Peru was 'annexed by the Viceroyalty of Peru as an emergency measure to stop the spread of the revolution' (1810) and stayed royalist until 1825.

capitals.name: Buenos Aires
capitals.note: Infobox 'Buenos Aires (1776-1811)'; the royalists moved to Montevideo after Elio declared Buenos Aires a rebel city on 19 January 1811.

capitals.name: Cordoba
capitals.note: Provisional capital from 14 July to August 1806 during the first British invasion.

capitals.name: Montevideo
capitals.note: Capital of the royalist rump until the surrender of 1814.

intersect.text: roughly today's Argentina, northern Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay and Uruguay

correction.text: the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata, 'roughly today's Argentina, northern Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay and Uruguay', as far as Spain held it

keyframe_review.note: The viceroyalty at creation: 'roughly today's Argentina, northern Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay and Uruguay'; governorates Rio de la Plata, Montevideo, Misiones Guaranies, Malvinas, Paraguay, Tucuman, Santa Cruz de la Sierra, Moxos, Chiquitos and Chucuito, and Charcas under its audiencia. The page gives no area; the shape is Cliopatria's Spanish Empire of 1778 inside those countries, so Patagonia and the Chaco, never held, are mostly outside. The Portuguese changes (1777, 1801) and Puno (1796) are ledger events.

correction.text: the royalist and Paraguayan remainder after the May Revolution

keyframe_review.note: After 25 May 1810 the Provinces follow the Primera Junta; Upper Peru goes to the Viceroyalty of Peru; Montevideo ('rejected the authority of the Primera Junta') and Paraguay ('rejected Buenos Aires' authority') remain with the royalist government.

correction.text: Montevideo and Colonia, the two places that stayed royalist

keyframe_review.note: The royalist rump: 'Montevideo and Colonia stayed royalist' after Las Piedras; Elio made Montevideo the capital. The Treaty of Pacification of 21 October 1811 'accepted Elio's authority over the Banda Oriental' and the siege was 'reestablished' on 20 October 1812, so the countryside was contested (ledger). The surrender followed in May-June 1814.

intersect.text: roughly today's Argentina, northern Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay and Uruguay

region.text: the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata, 'roughly today's Argentina, northern Chile, Bolivia, Paraguay and Uruguay', as far as Spain held it

ledger.note: 1776 (1 August): the Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata is organised. 'Organised: 1 August 1776': the king gave Cevallos 'control over the Audiencia of Charcas and the corregimiento of Cuyo'; the creation was 'formalised' on 27 October 1777, 'ending its temporary nature'.

region.text: Colonia del Sacramento and San Gabriel Island

ledger.note: 1777 (1 October): the Treaty of San Ildefonso confirms Colonia del Sacramento. 'Portugal recognised Spanish sovereignty over Colonia del Sacramento and San Gabriel Island.'

1777 (1 October): Spain gives up Santa Catalina and Rio Grande in the same treaty. 'Spain gave up Santa Catalina and Río Grande'; the page does not say they were part of the viceroyalty's governorates, which were organised a year earlier.
1796: Puno returns to Peru. 'In 1796, Puno became part of the Viceroyalty of Peru' (Chucuito had been a governorate of the Rio de la Plata from 1776).

region.text: the Misiones Orientales, the seven missions east of the Uruguay

ledger.note: 1801 (War of the Oranges): Portugal takes the Misiones Orientales. 'Portuguese forces and Guarani rebels took the Misiones Orientales' in 1801-1802; Portugal 'accepted to return the conquered territories to Spain, but never did so'. [Reviewer am-06-x, 2026-10-19: region narrowed to the Jesuit Missions inside Brazil (the page names only the Misiones Orientales; the whole region also covers Argentine Misiones and southern Paraguay) and counterpart set to colonial-brazil, whose 1801 gain is the mirror.]

region.text: Buenos Aires and the plain around it

ledger.note: 1806 (June): a British force takes Buenos Aires. 'Beresford took Buenos Aires in June'; the capital was provisionally moved to Cordoba (14 July to August 1806).

region.text: Buenos Aires and the plain around it

ledger.note: 1806 (August): Liniers retakes Buenos Aires. He 'recaptured it in 46 days' (La Reconquista) after Beresford took it in June, so in August; the month is derived from the page's 46 days and the day is not given.

region.text: Buenos Aires and the plain around it

ledger.note: 1807 (28 June): the second British invasion begins at the Rio de la Plata. 'The second invasion began on 28 June' (the page's earlier text has the British also in Montevideo, undated here).

region.text: Buenos Aires and the plain around it

ledger.note: 1807 (7 July): Whitelocke surrenders. 'Whitelocke surrendered on 7 July (La Defensa).'

region.text: Upper Peru: the intendancies of Chuquisaca, La Paz, Potosi and Cochabamba, plus Moxos and Chiquitos

ledger.note: 1810: Upper Peru is annexed to the Viceroyalty of Peru. It was 'annexed by the Viceroyalty of Peru as an emergency measure to stop the spread of the revolution' (the intendancies of Chuquisaca, La Paz, Potosi, Cochabamba, plus Moxos and Chiquitos). The page puts it in the year of the revolution without a month.

region.text: the Provinces that followed the Primera Junta

ledger.note: 1810 (25 May): the Primera Junta takes Buenos Aires and the Provinces. After an open cabildo voted 156 to 69 to dismiss Cisneros, the Junta was formed; the page names the junta's 'Provinces' but gives no list. The land is Cliopatria's Rio de la Plata shape of 1811.

region.text: Paraguay, which left the royalist side in 1811

ledger.note: 1811: Paraguay declares independence. 'The Intendency of Paraguay rejected Buenos Aires' authority, but declared independence a year later' (a year after 1810).

region.text: the Banda Oriental around royalist Montevideo

ledger.note: 1811 (28 February): the Banda Oriental rises. 'On 28 February 1811, the Cry of Asencio took place', an uprising against Elio led by Artigas; after Las Piedras the royalists held only Montevideo and Colonia. The Treaty of Pacification (21 October 1811) 'accepted Elio's authority', and on 20 October 1812 the siege of Montevideo was 'reestablished'.

1814: Montevideo falls. 'On 17 May 1814, Vigodet negotiated a surrender' and Alvear took the city on 23 May (text) or 23 June 1814 (infobox, 'Fall of Montevideo'); the page calls it 'the de facto ending' of the viceroyalty. Brown had won at Martin Garcia on 15 March and blockaded Montevideo from 20 April.

region.text: Montevideo and Colonia, the two places that stayed royalist

ledger.note: 1814 (23 June): the last royalist stronghold of the viceroyalty falls. The page: 'The Viceroyalty was disestablished in 1825 as Spanish political entity' and 'Formally abolished: 1 April 1825' (Olañeta's death at Tumusla), but the de facto end is the fall of Montevideo; Upper Peru had been Peru's since 1810.

wars.name: War of the Oranges (Misiones Orientales)
wars.outcome: Portugal took the Misiones Orientales and never returned them.

wars.name: British invasions of the Río de la Plata

zones.text: Buenos Aires and the plain around it

wars.outcome: Beresford held Buenos Aires for 46 days in 1806; Whitelocke surrendered on 7 July 1807.

wars.name: Banda Oriental campaign and siege of Montevideo
wars.outcome: Artigas's uprising (Cry of Asencio, 28 February 1811), the Treaty of Pacification (21 October 1811), the siege reestablished on 20 October 1812 and Vigodet's surrender on 17 May 1814.

certainty.note: Frontiers with Portuguese Brazil follow the 1777 Treaty of San Ildefonso for Colonia and San Gabriel; the Chaco and Patagonia limits are undefined.
The royalist rump after 1810 is a besieged city, not a frontier.

sources.title: Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
sources.note: Creation of 1776-77, territory by governorate, the 1777 and 1801 changes with Portugal, the British invasions, the May Revolution, Upper Peru, Paraguay, the Banda Oriental and the fall of Montevideo.

notes:
Written by am-06-x from one page (budget 2-5; the Peru and Peruvian independence pages were read for the siblings). Not settled:
(1) The page gives no area figure; the 1776 shape is Cliopatria's Spanish Empire of 1778 inside Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay, Uruguay and Antofagasta (the 'northern Chile' of the page): a gap-filler may want the Patagonian and Chaco claims separated.
(2) The page does not date the Audiencia of Buenos Aires and does not say Cuyo went back to Chile; Chile's dossier (captaincy-general-of-chile) is the other owner of Cuyo until 1776.
(3) End: infobox 23 June 1814, text 23 May 1814, surrender 17 May 1814, formal abolition 1 April 1825 (Olañeta): the dossier ends 1814-06. The royalist stronghold of Upper Peru is drawn under the Viceroyalty of Peru from 1810.
(4) Santa Catalina and Rio Grande: the page says Spain 'gave up' these in 1777 but does not say whether the viceroyalty administered them; recorded at confidence 2 as a loss.
(5) 'Federal League' (Cliopatria 1814-1819, Artigas) is not on this page; the Banda Oriental after 1814 belongs to the rio-de-la-plata and federal-league dossiers (am-08).
(6) The August 1806 month of Liniers's recapture is derived from the page's '46 days' after a June capture (confidence 2).
